subject: Private Deployment: Escrow Alternatives & Operator Evidence — MSA/Order Form Redlines
messages:
From: Paul Johnson <paul.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: sarah.lee@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-20T16:24:00Z
Subject: Private deployment - evidence & operator access questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and procurement teams reviewed the MSA and Order Form and flagged the private/on-prem addendum. Before we proceed to legal redlines, a few things we need clarified:

- What level of access will Redwood operators have in a VPC/on-prem deployment? We need a written boundary (network and console) and an attestation option.
- Are you able to provide an escrow-like proof of operational capability (attestation, snapshots, or HSM-backed key custody) if we require it for our regulated environment?
- Can you commit to an audit window and a schedule for forensic snapshots (frequency, retention)?

We attached a short requirements summary (Acme-Initial-Requirements.pdf). Please loop in your legal and product folks — we want to avoid a long redline cycle but ensure our auditors are comfortable.

Best,
Paul
Paul Johnson
Head of Infrastructure Security | Acme Health
paul.johnson@acmehealth.com

Attachment: Acme-Initial-Requirements.pdf (1 page, PDF summary)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Johnson <paul.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment - evidence & operator access questions

Paul — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Markus (legal) and Monica (solutions) to get concrete answers and proposed language for the addendum. High-level replies:

- Operator boundaries: we can commit to operator actions limited to provisioning/health/debugging; no full admin over customer application data. Monica will sketch the control-plane-only layout and runbook.
- Escrow alternatives: Redwood does not generally offer source-code escrow, but we have two common patterns we can propose:
  1) HSM-backed customer key custody + auditable attestations and signed snapshots of operator runbooks; or
  2) Quarterly operational attestations + encrypted snapshots deposited with a neutral custodian (we can work with Audit-ops-type providers).
- Audit window & snapshots: we can produce audit logs and periodic snapshots; need to align retention with your compliance needs.

Please find attached our initial list of ask/clarifying redlines (RNW-redlines-ask.docx). Markus — can you advise on acceptable contract language for the Order Form/MSA addenda? Monica — can you prepare a short architecture diagram that limits operator scope?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate a short sync if helpful.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: RNW-redlines-ask.docx

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Paul Johnson <paul.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment - evidence & operator access questions

Paul / Naomi — quick legal read: we can take the following positions and propose concrete language on the addendum and order form. Summary below, full positions attached as a PDF (Legal-positions.pdf).

1) License scope: customer receives perpetual runtime license to run the specified model artifacts in-customer environment; Redwood retains model IP. We can add explicit prohibitions on extracting model weights.
2) Operator access: we will accept a narrowly‑scoped operator role confined to monitored provisioning and incident-only debugging. All such actions will be logged and subject to forensic export on request.
3) Escrow/escrow-like evidence: we prefer not to escrow source, but we can provide attestations and an encrypted snapshot protocol: Redwood produces signed, time-stamped encrypted snapshots of runtime assets (not raw weights) and customer-managed encryption keys are held in their KMS or a neutral custodian; we can include an auditor access clause for a defined audit window.
4) Audit rights: standard cooperative audit clause with notice and scope limits; for on-site or full forensic audits we propose a commercial cadence (reasonable fees/time).

Open items for negotiation: whether customer requires unconditional on-site access (we prefer scheduled windows with pre-approved scope) and whether the snapshot contents meet the customer's compliance goals.

Next steps: Naomi and Monica to confirm technical scope for the operator role; I'll draft redline language for the addendum and the order form and share next week.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Legal-positions.pdf

From: Paul Johnson <paul.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: sarah.lee@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-23T11:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment - evidence & operator access questions

Markus — thanks for the clarity. A few follow-ups from our compliance team:

- The phrase "not raw weights" needs definition. We will require that any snapshot or artifact cannot be used to reconstruct the model to a degree that impacts our regulatory posture. Can you add a non-reverse-engineering assurance?
- On-site audits: we appreciate scheduled windows, but for critical incidents we require an emergency access path — e.g., 48-hour notice maximum. Can you confirm?
- Custody: we'd prefer the encryption keys for the encrypted snapshot to be escrowed by a neutral custodian under a dual-key split with Acme and the custodian so Acme can trigger release under narrow conditions.

Attached our list of follow-up questions (Acme-questions.xlsx).

Paul

Attachment: Acme-questions.xlsx

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Johnson <paul.johnson@acmehealth.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T08:58:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment - evidence & operator access questions

Paul — quick technical note to address the reverse-engineering and operator access concerns. (Quoting below some lines from Markus for context.)

> 1) License scope: customer receives perpetual runtime license to run the specified model artifacts in-customer environment; Redwood retains model IP.
> 2) Operator access: we will accept a narrowly‑scoped operator role confined to monitored provisioning and incident-only debugging.

Attached: Operator-Boundary-Diagram.png (diagram). Key points:
- Operator role: CLI + control-plane reprovisioning only. No shell-level access to customer app hosts.
- Snapshots we can provide are operational artifacts (container images with hashes, metadata, dependency manifests) but not raw weight dumps. Those artifacts are versioned and signed by Redwood.
- For emergency incidents, we can support a 48-hour emergency access protocol that requires joint signing by customer security and Redwood's on-call + a narrow scope statement. All emergency actions will be fully recorded and forensically exported to Acme.

On custody: Diego — can you start a conversation with the neutral custodian we work with (audit-ops@securevault.com) about the dual-key split? If custodian agrees, we can propose that in the addendum.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the diagram.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Operator-Boundary-Diagram.png

Paul — thanks everyone for the fast turn. Summary and next steps: 

1) Redwood will draft a private-deploy addendum that:
   - Defines license scope and explicit anti-reverse-engineering language for snapshots;
   - Limits operator role to control-plane actions with an emergency 48-hour access protocol and full forensic logging;
   - Describes encrypted snapshot protocol with dual-key custody as an escrow alternative (we will confirm custodian feasibility).
2) Markus will circulate a redline of the MSA + Order Form addendum by EOD 2026-11-03.
3) Diego to initiate custodian outreach with Audit-ops (cc'd internally) and report back by 2026-11-02.
4) Naomi to schedule a 30-minute sync with Acme and Redwood legal/solutions for 2026-11-04 (calendar invite to follow).

Paul — does that plan look acceptable? If so, we'll treat this as the path to a clean signature once redlines converge.

Thanks —
Naomi
